Drop empty or constant columns and rows

Source: R/dsc.R
drp.Rd

drpempty() removes rows or columns that are entirely missing. drpconst() removes columns that hold a single distinct value. Use them after reading a spreadsheet export, which often carries blank padding rows, empty columns and columns that repeat one value (a year, a jurisdiction) on every row.

Usage

drpempty(data, which = c("rows", "cols"), quiet = FALSE)

drpconst(data, naasval = FALSE, quiet = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A data frame whose empty rows or columns are dropped.

which

"rows", "cols", or both (the default, c("rows", "cols")).

quiet

Logical: TRUE skips the summary of what was dropped (rows and columns before and after, the columns removed), which is otherwise sent through message(); default FALSE.

naasval

Logical: treat NA as a distinct value, so a column of NAs plus one real value counts as two (default FALSE).

Value

The data frame, with the offending rows or columns removed. The names of the columns that were dropped are attached as the "dropped" attribute (a character vector, empty when none); dropped rows are not listed.

Details

A constant column carries no information and breaks anything that scales by variance, so it is worth removing – but it is also a FINDING. A column that was informative in an earlier release and is constant in a fresh one means the source changed, so check that before deleting it and moving on.

drpempty() removes all-NA columns first, then all-NA rows among the remaining columns, and resets the row names. An empty string is a value, not missing. drpconst() counts the distinct non-missing values of each column (with naasval = TRUE, NA counts as a value), so an all-NA column is also dropped by default. Neither function modifies anything in place.

Errors: data not a data frame (or with missing or duplicated names); which other than "rows" and/or "cols".

See also

profcols, which reports n_distinct without removing anything.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  keep = c(1, 2, NA),
  allna = c(NA, NA, NA),
  constant = c(7, 7, 7)
)

drpempty(df)
#> -- Empty rows and columns dropped
#>    rows 3 -> 3, columns 3 -> 2
#>    columns dropped (all missing): allna
#>   keep constant
#> 1    1        7
#> 2    2        7
#> 3   NA        7
attr(drpempty(df), "dropped")
#> -- Empty rows and columns dropped
#>    rows 3 -> 3, columns 3 -> 2
#>    columns dropped (all missing): allna
#> [1] "allna"

drpconst(df)
#> -- Constant columns dropped
#>    columns 3 -> 1
#>    columns dropped (one value): allna, constant
#>   keep
#> 1    1
#> 2    2
#> 3   NA
attr(drpconst(df), "dropped")
#> -- Constant columns dropped
#>    columns 3 -> 1
#>    columns dropped (one value): allna, constant
#> [1] "allna"    "constant"

# Rows only.
drpempty(data.frame(a = c(1, NA), b = c(2, NA)), which = "rows")
#> -- Empty rows and columns dropped
#>    rows 2 -> 1, columns 2 -> 2
#>   a b
#> 1 1 2

# A column of NAs plus one value is constant by default, and not when
# NA is treated as a value of its own.
x <- data.frame(v = c(NA, NA, 5))
ncol(drpconst(x))
#> -- Constant columns dropped
#>    columns 1 -> 0
#>    columns dropped (one value): v
#> [1] 0
ncol(drpconst(x, naasval = TRUE))
#> -- Constant columns dropped
#>    columns 1 -> 1
#> [1] 1

# only data frames
try(drpempty(c(1, NA)))
#> Error : drpempty: `data` must be a data frame.
